scope: kanji meanings EN + pt-BR, N5-N1 (2131 records)

findings.issue: 'school' is the meaning of the compound 学校, not of the character 学 itself (standard glosses: study, learning, science). It also breaks EN-PT alignment: pt has 'ciência' (science), which the EN list does not cover, while 'escola' is absent from pt.
notes: KANJIDIC2 glosses 学 as study/learning/science; pt list (estudo, aprender, ciência) tracks that, so en's 'school' breaks EN-PT alignment and drifts from the Layer-A source. Fix is correct.

EN 'school' breaks alignment with pt ('ciência' uncovered) and deviates from the KANJIDIC2 gloss set (study, learning, science). Fix 'study, learning, science' is correct, though 学 does carry a school sense in 大学/中学.

findings.issue: 'pouco' means a small QUANTITY (few/not much), which is the meaning of 少, not 小. 小 means small in SIZE. The EN gloss 'little' (small-sized) was mistranslated as quantity, which will directly collide with 少 (sukunai/pouco) when the learner meets it.
notes: 'pouco' is quantity-only in PT (gloss of 少, cf. 少し/少ない); 小 is size. 'Little' here = small-sized, so 'pequeno' alone is the correct gloss. Real 小/少 collision for learners.
小 is size-smallness (ちいさい); pt 'pouco' is quantity-only in Portuguese and belongs to 少 (sukunai). Real sense mistranslation of EN 'little'; fix 'pequeno' is correct.

findings.issue: Gloss 'sound (a sound)' is not a recognized core sense of 発 and is redundant with 'emit' (発する = emit light/sound/words). It also breaks EN-pt alignment: pt 'disparar' renders the real sense 'fire/discharge (a shot)' (発射/発砲, counter for gunshots), which the EN list lacks.
notes: 'sound (a sound)' is not a dictionary sense of 発 (redundant with 'emit'), and slot 4 misaligns with pt 'disparar' (=fire/discharge, 発射/発砲, はな(つ)). Suggested 'fire (a shot)' is correct.
'sound (a sound)' is unattested in authoritative glosses for 発 and misaligns with pt[3] 'disparar' (fire/discharge, cf. kun はな(つ) in readings_fact); 'fire (a shot)' is the correct fix.

findings.issue: 'study' is the meaning of the compound 勉強, not of the character 強 itself. 強 means strong / force / coerce (強いる); listing 'study' teaches a false character meaning.
notes: 'study' is only the meaning of 勉強; no dictionary glosses the character 強 as 'study'. Readings include し (強いる), so 'coerce' is a grounded replacement (or simply drop the third sense).
No authoritative source (KANJIDIC2, Nelson) lists 'study' for 強; it means strong/force/compel (強いる, kun し in readings_fact). 'study' is 勉強-only. 'coerce' is a valid replacement.

findings.issue: 'estudar' mirrors the compound-derived error in EN: 強 by itself never means 'estudar' (that is 勉強). Should be dropped or replaced by the coerce sense.
notes: 'estudar' mirrors the same compound-derived error; the character alone never means it. 'coagir' correctly renders 強いる.
'estudar' mirrors the same compound-derived error; 強 alone never means estudar. 'coagir' correctly renders the 強いる sense and is natural pt-BR.

findings.issue: The pt list drops the core sense 'commute' (通う, go regularly/attend) that EN presents as core; 'passar/atravessar/tráfego' do not cover it.
notes: EN lists 'commute' (通う) as a core sense but pt has no equivalent; 'passar/atravessar/tráfego' don't cover it. Adding 'frequentar' restores locale parity and matches 学校に通う usage.
EN curates 'commute' as a core sense (通う, staple N4 usage 学校に通う); pt 'passar/atravessar/tráfego' cannot express habitual attendance. 'frequentar' restores locale parity.

findings.issue: '-tico' is not a recognized Portuguese suffix; the adjectival suffix is '-ico' (como em científico, sistemático), the natural counterpart of EN '-ical'.
notes: '-tico' is not a recognized pt suffix; dictionaries list '-ico' (científico, econômico), the natural counterpart of 的/-ical. The 't' belongs to the stem, not the suffix.
Portuguese grammars/Houaiss recognize '-ico' (científico, econômico) and '-ático', never '-tico'; presenting a nonexistent suffix in learner-facing content is a real defect.

findings.issue: 'ânimo' (mood/disposition) does not render EN 'mind' and skews the sense; 'mente' keeps the pt list aligned with the curated EN sense set.
notes: 'ânimo' (mood/energy/disposition) mistranslates the curated EN sense 'mind' and skews toward 気/意気; 'mente' matches 意識/意中 and keeps pt aligned with the Layer-A-sourced en set.
Modern pt-BR 'ânimo' means mood/energy/encouragement, not 'mind'; it misleads for core N4 uses (意識, 注意) and breaks parity with the curated EN sense. 'mente' aligns correctly.

findings.issue: Bare transitive 'despedir' in pt-BR primarily means 'to fire/dismiss someone (from a job)'. The 'see off' sense of 送 (見送る) needs the reflexive 'despedir-se (de)' or a gloss like 'acompanhar (quem parte)'; as listed it can teach a wrong meaning.
notes: Bare transitive 'despedir' in pt-BR means 'to fire (an employee)'; the 'see off' sense of 送 requires pronominal 'despedir-se (de)'. As listed it teaches the wrong meaning.
Bare transitive 'despedir' in pt-BR = fire/dismiss; the 'see off' (見送る) sense requires pronominal 'despedir-se (de)'. As a standalone gloss it teaches a wrong meaning. Suggested fix is good.

findings.issue: 'important' is the meaning of the compound 大切 (taisetsu), not of 切 itself; the character's own senses are 'cut' and 'earnest/keen/acute'. Presenting 'important' as a core meaning of the single character is misleading. pt 'importante' mirrors this and should be fixed in parallel.
findings.fix: Remove 'important' (en) and 'importante' (pt), keeping 'cut, earnest' / 'cortar, sério'. If a third gloss is desired, use 'sharp' / 'afiado' (KANJIDIC2 'be sharp') rather than 'keen, acute', which is redundant with 'earnest'.
notes: No authoritative source (KANJIDIC2, Halpern, Kanjipedia) lists 'important' for 切 alone; it is the compound meaning of 大切. 'keen, acute' matches Halpern; pt 'importante' must be fixed in parallel.
'Important' is a 大切-only sense; KANJIDIC2 gives 'cut, cutoff, be sharp' and kanwa dicts give cut/earnest/pressing/all — no 'important'. But the suggested 'keen, acute' duplicates 'earnest'.

findings.issue: 'matter' is not a meaning of 仕. It belongs to 事 (the second character of 仕事). 仕 itself means 'serve/attend' (仕える) and is used for 'do' (する) in 仕事/仕方. Teaching 'matter' assigns another character's meaning to 仕.
notes: 'matter' belongs to 事, not 仕 (attend/serve/do per KANJIDIC-class sources); real meaning contamination. Fix 'serve, do' is correct.
'Matter' is 事's meaning, not 仕's. KANJIDIC-lineage glosses for 仕 are attend/doing/official/serve; no source gives 'matter'. Genuinely wrong and misleading for 仕事 decomposition.

findings.issue: 'assunto' translates the erroneous EN sense 'matter', which belongs to 事, not 仕. It propagates a false meaning into the pt-BR gloss list.
notes: 'assunto' merely translates the erroneous 'matter' sense; must be dropped alongside it. Fix 'servir, fazer' is correct.
'assunto' directly translates the erroneous 'matter' sense into the learner-facing pt-BR list; falls with the EN error.

findings.issue: 'noitada' in pt-BR means a night out / all-night partying, not 'night/evening'. It is a misleading colloquial sense presented as a core meaning of 夜. 'noite' alone covers both EN senses.
notes: 'noitada' means a night out/partying in pt-BR, not 'evening'; misleading as a core gloss of 夜. 'noite' covers both EN senses.
pt-BR 'noitada' dominantly means night out/all-nighter/farra, not 'evening'. As a core gloss of 夜 it teaches a false association; 'noite' alone covers both EN senses.

findings.issue: The pt list omits the 'ease/comfort' sense (ラク, as in 楽な = easy, comfortable), which the EN list includes as core and which is must-know at this level. 'prazer' renders pleasure/fun, not ease.
notes: PT list drops the ラク ease/comfort sense present in the record's own EN list (4 vs 3 senses), breaking parity; 'conforto' is an acceptable addition.
pt list omits the ラク sense (ease/comfort, 楽な), a core N4 sense present in EN. 'prazer' does not cover it. Real locale-parity gap; 'conforto' is an adequate fix.

findings.issue: 'study hard' is the meaning of the compound 勉強, not of the character 勉 itself, which means exertion/effort/diligence. Presenting a compound's sense as a core character meaning is misleading; the pt list correctly omits it, so EN and pt are also misaligned.
notes: KANJIDIC2 gives exertion/endeavour for 勉; 'study hard' comes only from the compound 勉強. Kun つと(める)=exert oneself. The pt list has no equivalent, so en/pt are misaligned. Suggested fix is good.
'study hard' is a 勉強-compound sense, not a KANJIDIC meaning of 勉; pt list (diligência/esforço/empenho) omits it, so en/pt are misaligned. Suggested fix is correct.

findings.issue: Missing the primary sense 'roof' (also 'house'): 屋根 (roof) and 屋上 (rooftop) are common N5/N4 words a learner must decode with this character. If added, pt should gain 'telhado' as well.
notes: 'Roof' is the lead KANJIDIC2 sense of 屋 (roof, house, shop, dealer) and is needed for N4/N5 words 屋根/屋上; current list only covers the -や suffix senses. Add 'roof' to en and 'telhado' to pt.
KANJIDIC lists roof/house as primary senses of 屋; the オク reading in readings_fact maps to that sense (屋上/屋根 are N4). Add 'roof' to en and 'telhado' to pt.

findings.issue: 'kanji' is the meaning of the compound 漢字, not of the character 漢 itself. 漢 alone means Han (dynasty)/China (also 'fellow/man' in compounds). Presenting 'kanji' as a core meaning teaches the compound's sense as the character's.
notes: No authoritative source (KANJIDIC2, JMdict, Jitenon) lists 'kanji' as a sense of 漢 alone; it is the sense of the compound 漢字. Suggested fix matches KANJIDIC2 (Sino-/China) and is fine.
漢 alone means Han/China (KANJIDIC2: 'Sino-, China'); 'kanji' is the sense of the compound 漢字. Listing it as a character meaning is a factual error; the suggested fix is acceptable.

findings.issue: Mirrors the EN defect: 'kanji' is the sense of the compound 漢字, not of 漢 alone. The pt list should render the character's own senses (Han/China).
notes: pt list mirrors the en defect: 'kanji' is the compound 漢字's sense, not the character's. 'chinês (Han), China' correctly renders the character's own senses.
pt mirrors the en defect: 'kanji' is not a sense of 漢 itself. 'chinês (Han), China' correctly renders the character's own senses.

findings.issue: 'economy' is the meaning of the compound 経済, not of the character 済 itself (settle a debt, relieve, finish, come to an end). Presenting it as a core character meaning teaches a compound sense as if it were the kanji's own.
notes: KANJIDIC2 3.6.2 (repo Layer-A source) lists settle/relieve/finish/come to an end — no 'economy'; that sense belongs to the compound 経済. Suggested fix matches authoritative senses.
KANJIDIC2 gives settle/relieve/finish/come to an end for 済; 'economy' exists only via the compound 経済. Compound-sense leak into a character entry; suggested fix matches Layer-A senses.

findings.issue: 'economia' mirrors the defective EN gloss 'economy', which belongs to the compound 経済 and not to 済 itself; the pt list should drop it in line with the EN fix.
notes: 'economia' mirrors the defective en gloss; must drop with the en fix. 'socorrer' is a valid pt-BR for 'relieve (burden)' (救済), though 'aliviar' also works.
'economia' mirrors the defective EN gloss and must drop with it; 'socorrer' correctly renders the 'relieve (burden)' sense (救済) in pt-BR.

findings.issue: 'new' is not a core meaning of 初 (first time, beginning) and invites confusion with 新 (new), an N5 kanji; standard references (KANJIDIC2, Jisho) do not list 'new'. The pt side correctly uses 'inicial', not 'novo'.
notes: KANJIDIC2 gives only 'first time, beginning' — no 'new'; 'new' collides with 新 (N5) and breaks en/pt parity since pt already says 'inicial'. Suggested 'initial' restores alignment.
KANJIDIC2/Jisho list only 'first time, beginning' for 初; all kun readings mean first/initial. 'new' belongs to 新 (N5) and breaks EN/PT parity (pt already says 'inicial', not 'novo').

findings.issue: EN lists four core senses (direct, straight, fix, honest) but the pt list drops 'honest' (honesto/franco), a real core sense of 直 (as in 正直). Brazilian learners lose a sense the EN curation presents as core, breaking EN-pt alignment.
notes: pt list really drops the 'honest' sense present in en (直 as in 正直/素直); all other batch entries keep 1:1 EN-PT sense parity. Suggested fix 'honesto' is correct pt-BR.
Batch confirms en has 4 senses incl. 'honest' but pt only 3; every other aligned item keeps 1:1 parity. 'Honesto' is a real core sense (正直/素直), so the drop is a genuine EN-pt misalignment.

findings.issue: EN presents 'case' (grammatical/legal sense, e.g. 格助詞) as a core sense of 格, but the pt list has no equivalent, so the sense sets are misaligned.
notes: 'case' (grammatical, 格助詞) is a distinct EN sense with no PT counterpart — not a synonym collapse — breaking en/pt sense parity; 'caso (gramatical)' is a correct pt-BR fix.

EN lists 'case' (a distinct sense: 格助詞/主格) with no pt counterpart. Unlike 割/難, this is a dropped sense, not a synonym merge; 'caso (gramatical)' is correct pt-BR and the batch already uses parentheticals (passar (tempo)).

findings.issue: 'word' is not a meaning of 葉 itself; it comes from the compound 言葉. Dictionaries gloss 葉 only as leaf/blade/counter for flat things. The batch elsewhere marks compound-bound senses (e.g. 残 'regret (in 残念)'), so an unmarked 'word' presents a compound meaning as core.
notes: EN: no reference glosses 葉 as 'word' (KANJIDIC2: leaf/blade/counter). Sense exists only in 言葉; batch convention (残 'regret (in 残念)') requires the marker.

No reference (KANJIDIC2, Kodansha, Nelson) glosses 葉 as 'word'; it glosses leaf/blade/counter for flat things. 'Word' is 言葉-bound, and the batch's own convention (残 'regret (in 残念)') requires the marker.

findings.issue: 'palavra' mirrors the EN defect: it is the meaning of the compound 言葉, not of the character 葉 (folha). Needs the same compound marker used elsewhere in the corpus (cf. 残 'pena (em 残念)').
notes: PT mirrors EN: 'palavra' is the sense of 言葉, not of 葉 alone. Marker '(em 言葉)' matches corpus precedent 'pena (em 残念)'.
Mirrors the EN defect: 'palavra' is the sense of the compound 言葉, not of 葉 (folha). Marking '(em 言葉)' matches the corpus convention already used for 残 'pena (em 残念)'.

findings.issue: 'worry' is the meaning of the compound 心配, not of 配 itself (distribute, deliver, allot, arrange; also spouse/exile). No reference lists 'worry' for the standalone character; presenting it unmarked teaches a compound meaning as core.
notes: EN: references gloss 配 as distribute/spouse/exile/rationing; くばる = distribute. 'Worry' is compound-bound (心配) and must carry the marker.
KANJIDIC2/Nelson/Spahn gloss 配 as distribute/allot/spouse/exile/rationing — none list 'worry'. The sense is compositional from 心配 (心を配る), so it must carry the compound marker per batch convention.

findings.issue: 'preocupação' mirrors the EN defect: it is the sense of the compound 心配, not of 配 (distribuir/dispor/entregar). Needs the compound marker or removal.
notes: PT mirrors EN: 'preocupação' is the sense of 心配, not of 配 standalone. '(em 心配)' marker fix is correct.
Mirrors EN: 'preocupação' is the 心配 sense, not a sense of 配 (distribuir/dispor). '(em 心配)' marker matches the established 残念 format.

findings.issue: 'natural' is the meaning of compounds like 自然/天然, not of 然 itself, which means 'so, thus, in that manner / -like (state suffix)'. References (KANJIDIC, Kodansha KLD) gloss it 'sort of thing, so, if so' with no 'natural'.
notes: EN: KANJIDIC/KLD gloss 然 as 'so, thus, sort of thing / state suffix'; 'natural' arises only compositionally in 自然/天然. Marker '(in 自然)' is the right fix.

然 means 'so, thus, in that state / -like suffix'; no dictionary (KANJIDIC2 'sort of thing, so, if so', Henshall 'so, like that') lists 'natural'. That reading is compositional in 自然/天然/当然, so it needs the marker.

findings.issue: 'natural' mirrors the EN defect: sense of the compound 自然, not of the character 然 (assim, deste modo, '-como' de estado). Needs the compound marker or removal.
findings.suggested: assim, deste modo, natural (em 自然)
findings.fix: assim, deste modo, natural (em 自然)
notes: PT mirrors EN: 'natural' unmarked teaches a false standalone sense; '(em 自然)' marker fix is correct.
Mirrors EN: 'natural' vem de compostos (自然/天然), não do caractere 然 (assim, deste modo). Marker '(em 自然)' is consistent with corpus convention.

findings.issue: 'prosperity' is not a meaning of 景 (scenery, view, scene; bright). It is loosely derived from 景気, which itself means 'business conditions' (prosperity only in 好景気). No reference lists 'prosperity' for this character; misleading as a core sense.
notes: EN: KANJIDIC2 glosses 景 only as scenery/view. 'Prosperity' is doubly indirect (景気 = business conditions; prosperity = 好景気), so removal (not a marker) is right.

No reference lists 'prosperity' for 景 (scenery, view, scene, bright); even 景気 is neutral 'business conditions' (prosperity only in 好景気). Removal, as suggested, is the right fix — a compound marker would still be inaccurate.

findings.issue: 'prosperidade' mirrors the EN defect: 景 means paisagem/vista/cena; 'prosperidade' comes indirectly from 景気 and is not a sense of the character.
notes: PT mirrors EN: 'prosperidade' is not a sense of 景; even '(em 景気)' would be inaccurate. Removing it, leaving 'paisagem, vista', is correct.
Mirrors EN: 'prosperidade' is not a sense of 景 (paisagem/vista) and is two derivational steps away (好景気). Dropping it, as suggested, is correct.

findings.issue: 'candidate' is the meaning of the compound 候補 (kouho), not of the character 候 itself. Standard references (KANJIDIC2, Jisho) gloss 候 as climate/season/weather/wait for/expect; presenting 'candidate' as a core character meaning is misleading.
notes: KANJIDIC2/Jisho gloss 候 as climate/season/weather/wait for/expect; 'candidate' is the sense of the compound 候補, not the character. Suggested fix matches Layer-A sources.
KANJIDIC2 glosses 候 as climate/season/weather/wait for/expect; 'candidate' belongs to the compound 候補 only. Listing it as a character meaning violates the Layer-A fact rule.

findings.issue: 'candidato' mirrors the defective English entry: it is the sense of the compound 候補, not of the character 候. The pt list should drop it, keeping the climate/season senses.
notes: 'candidato' mirrors the same compound-only sense and must go. Suggested pt fix drops 'weather' parity with the en list, so add 'tempo'.
'candidato' mirrors the same compound-derived error; dropping it and keeping 'clima, estação' (optionally 'aguardar') is correct pt-BR.

findings.issue: Third pt item 'arriscar' is a verb ('to take a risk'), which is not a sense of 危. The EN list has three adjectives (dangerous/risky/perilous); 危 expresses a state of danger, never the action of risking something. Wrong POS and shifted sense.
notes: 'arriscar' (to take/put at risk) is not a sense of 危; its only verbal kun is あやぶむ 'temer/duvidar'. It also breaks the adjective pattern of the EN list. 'perigoso, arriscado' is the right fix.
'arriscar' (verb, to take a risk) is not a sense of 危 (あぶない/あやうい/あやぶむ = state of danger, fear); wrong POS vs the adjective-only EN list. But the fix must keep the batch's 1:1 en-pt slot parity.

findings.issue: 'sessão' (a scheduled session/showing) does not render EN 'gathering'; the 座 sense (一座, 座を盛り上げる) is a social gathering/company of people. 'reunião' is the faithful pt-BR rendering.
notes: 'sessão' in pt-BR means a cinema showing or formal deliberative session, not a social gathering (一座/座が白ける). Standard JA-PT glosses use 'reunião'; the suggested fix is correct.
pt-BR 'sessão' = session/showing, not 'gathering'; 座's sense (一座, assembled company) is 'reunião'. As-is it teaches a false 座=session mapping; suggested fix is correct.

findings.issue: 'midway' is the meaning of the compound 途中, not of the character 途 itself, which means way/road/route (cf. 用途, 前途, 途上). A compound sense is presented as a core character meaning.
notes: KANJIDIC2 glosses 途 as route/way/road only; 'midway' derives the 'mid' from 中 in 途中/中途, not from 途. Compound sense wrongly presented as a character meaning.
KANJIDIC2 glosses 途 as exactly 'route, way, road' — no 'midway'. The midway sense comes from 中 in 途中/中途, not from 途. Compound sense leaked into a core character meaning.

findings.issue: 'meio do caminho' mirrors the compound-derived sense of 途中 rather than a meaning of the character 途 (caminho/rota); should be dropped or replaced with a genuine character sense.
notes: 'meio do caminho' mirrors the same 途中-derived defect in pt-BR; replace with a genuine character sense consistent with the corrected en list.
'meio do caminho' mirrors the same 途中-derived defect and must go. But 'estrada' in the suggested fix over-concretizes (途 is abstract: 用途, 前途, 途上); 'rota' is the safer third gloss.

findings.issue: 'rude' in pt-BR is read primarily as 'impolite', which misrenders the 'harsh/stern' sense of 険 (as in 険しい顔). 'severo' or 'áspero' is the natural equivalent.
notes: pt-BR 'rude' defaults to impolite/grosseiro; 険's harsh sense is stern/grim (険しい顔), never discourtesy. Contextless gloss misleads; 'severo' is correct.
KANJIDIC2 sense is 'sharp eyes' (stern look, 険しい顔). Bare 'rude' in pt-BR reads as 'impolite' — a meaning 険 never has — creating a false association. 'severo' is the correct professional gloss.

findings.issue: Bare 'passar' in a gloss list reads as 'to pass' and fails to convey 'drop by' (立ち寄る); needs a clarifying form such as 'dar uma passada' or 'passar (em um lugar)'.
notes: Bare 'passar' reads as generic 'to pass' (過/通 semantics); 'aproximar-se, passar' even suggests passing by. Multiword glosses are house style, so 'dar uma passada' fits.
KANJIDIC2 sense is 'stop in'. Bare 'passar' reads as generic 'to pass' and invites conflation with 通る/過ぎる; the drop-by sense needs a frame. 'dar uma passada' is natural, unambiguous pt-BR.

findings.issue: EN presents four core senses (hang, hook, multiply, spend) but pt omits the 'spend/cost' sense (お金・時間がかかる), a must-know use of this kanji at N3. The pt list fails to cover the EN core sense set.
notes: EN core sense 'spend' (お金・時間がかかる/かける) has no pt counterpart; real coverage gap, and 'gastar' is the correct pt-BR rendering.
Verified in batch: en lists 4 senses incl. 'spend' but pt has only 3; the spend/cost sense (お金・時間をかける) is missing. 'gastar' is a correct pt-BR rendering.

findings.issue: EN 'grandparent' is gender-neutral, but pt 'avô' means only grandfather, narrowing the sense (祖母 = avó). A gender-inclusive rendering is needed.
notes: 'avô' = grandfather only; 祖 covers 祖父 AND 祖母, so the neutral EN 'grandparent' is narrowed. 'avô/avó' is the standard pt-BR fix.
Singular 'avô' = grandfather only (generic use is plural 'avós'); narrows the neutral EN 'grandparent' and misleads given 祖母 = avó. 'avô/avó' fixes it.

findings.issue: For the intransitive sense 'stray/go astray', standard pt-BR requires the pronominal form 'desviar-se'; bare 'desviar' reads as transitive 'to divert'. Also inconsistent with the reflexive style used elsewhere in the list (perder-se).
notes: pt-BR does NOT require the pronominal: intransitive 'desviar (de)' is standard Brazilian usage (Houaiss/Aulete). Claim is wrong; consistency point is purely stylistic.
Overstated: pt-BR accepts intransitive 'desviar' (Michaelis/Houaiss list vtd/vint/vpr; 'desviou do caminho' is standard). Bare infinitive gloss is defensible; purely stylistic.

findings.issue: "metrópole administrativa" mistranslates "urban prefecture" (confuses 府 with 都, the actual metropolis unit); "prefeitura" is a false-cognate risk in pt-BR (city hall) and clashes with 県 being glossed as "província" elsewhere in this dictionary.
findings.suggested: repartição do governo, província urbana (ex.: Osaka, Quioto)
findings.fix: repartição pública, província urbana (ex.: Osaka, Quioto)
notes: 府 is the urban-prefecture unit (Osaka/Kyoto), not the metropolis (都); 'metrópole administrativa' is factually wrong, and 'prefeitura' clashes with 県='província' in this same batch.

Verified: 県="província" in same batch, so "prefeitura" (municipal-level in pt-BR) clashes and misleads; "metrópole" is 都's designation, not 府's. Suggested fix is sound; unequal en/pt list lengths already exist in batch.

findings.issue: The pt list contains the identical word "par" twice; the bare second "par" (meant for the "pair/couple" sense, cf. 配偶) is indistinguishable from "par (número)". Differentiate with "casal" or "dupla".
notes: Verbatim duplicate 'par' in the pt list; the bare second 'par' (mate sense, cf. 配偶) is indistinguishable from 'par (número)'. Fix is sound; strictly only the last item must become 'casal'.

Duplicate "par" confirmed in data; bare second "par" is uninformative next to "par (número)" — real defect. But fix's casual→acidental swap is an unneeded drive-by: "casual" is correct pt-BR for the by-chance sense.

findings.issue: 'prepare' is the meaning of the compound 準備, not of 準 itself (準 = standard, level, conform to, semi-). Presenting it as core is misleading; the must-know 'semi-/quasi-' sense (準決勝, 準優勝) is also missing.
notes: 'prepare' belongs to 備 in 準備, not to 準; no authoritative source (KANJIDIC, Halpern, Nelson) glosses 準 as 'prepare', and the productive 'semi-' sense (準決勝, 準急) is missing.
'prepare' is compound-derived (準備), absent from KANJIDIC2/Halpern/Nelson for the standalone kanji; productive 'semi-' sense (準決勝, 準急) is missing. Suggested fix is correct.

findings.issue: Mirrors the EN defect: 'preparar' comes from the compound 準備, not from 準 itself, and the core 'semi-/quase-' sense (準決勝 = semifinal) is missing.
notes: Mirrors the EN defect: 'preparar' is compound-derived, 'semi-' missing. Suggested fix drops the 'conform to' sense kept in the EN fix, breaking EN-pt parity.
'preparar' mirrors the EN defect; 'semi-' missing. But the suggested fix drops 'conform to', breaking parity with the EN fix.

findings.issue: The pt list omits the 'frame' sense (額 = picture frame, as in 額縁) that the EN list presents as a core sense, breaking EN-pt sense-set alignment.
notes: EN has 4 distinct senses, pt has 3; 'frame' (額縁) is a real distinct sense, and this is the only record in the batch dropping a whole sense rather than a synonym. 'moldura' is correct.
'framed picture' is a genuine KANJIDIC2 core sense of 額 (額縁); EN carries it, pt omits it, violating the project's EN↔pt sense-set parity rule. 'moldura' is the right gloss.

findings.issue: 'specialty' is the meaning of the compound 専門, not of 門 itself. Standalone 門 means gate; extended senses are 'school (of thought), division/branch'. Presenting 'specialty' as a core meaning of 門 misleads learners (専, in this same batch, already carries 'specialize').
notes: No major kanji reference (KANJIDIC, Halpern, Nelson) glosses 門 as 'specialty' — they give gate / school (of a master) / branch of learning. 'Specialty' is 専門's compound meaning; misleading next to 専='specialize'.
KANJIDIC2: 門 = 'gate, counter for cannons' only; 'specialty' is KANJIDIC2's keyword for 専 (専門 leak). 'school (of thought)' (一門/門下) is a valid extended sense to keep a second gloss.

findings.issue: 'especialidade' mirrors the defective EN 'specialty' — that is 専門's meaning, not 門's. Should follow the corrected EN sense set.
notes: 'especialidade' inherits the defective EN sense; once EN becomes 'school (of thought)' the pt-BR must follow. 'escola (de pensamento)' is a correct rendering.
'especialidade' mirrors the misassigned EN gloss and must follow the EN correction; 'escola (de pensamento)' is natural pt-BR.

findings.issue: 'aproximar-se' (to approach) does not render 'adjoin' and suggests 接 means 'to approach' (that is 近づく). 接する means to touch/border/be adjacent. A learner would internalize a wrong core sense.
notes: 'aproximar-se' denotes movement toward (近づく/接近), not the state of adjoining. 接する = touch/border/be adjacent; JMdict gives 'to border on, to adjoin'. 'ser adjacente' is a correct pt-BR fix.
Layer A: 接 = touch/contact/adjoin/piece together. 'aproximar-se' encodes motion toward (近づく/接近する), not contact/adjacency; it mistranslates 'adjoin'. 'ser adjacente' is correct.

findings.issue: PT list drops the EN core sense 'certificate' (証券, 商品券) and substitutes 'passe', a compound-level usage (定期券). Sense sets should align; add/replace with 'certificado'.
notes: 'certificate' is a core sense of 券 (証券, 株券, 商品券; the character originally means a deed/tally) and pt drops it while 'passe' just duplicates the ticket sense. Layer-B pt must render the Layer-A EN set; 'certificado' fixes it.
pt-BR is Layer B derived from the en source list; 'passe' duplicates 'bilhete' while dropping the distinct 'certificate' sense (証券/商品券). Minor but real alignment defect; add 'certificado'.

findings.issue: EN 'shellfish' (the animals, as in 魚介類) is rendered as 'concha', which in pt-BR means the shell itself (the hard casing) or a ladle, not the animal. The correct rendering is 'marisco(s)'. As written it teaches a shifted sense (shell = 貝殻, not 介).
notes: 'Concha' means the shell casing in pt-BR, never the shellfish animal (魚介類 sense). 'Marisco' is the correct rendering; as written it teaches a shifted sense.
'Concha' = the shell casing or a ladle in pt-BR, not the animal; en gloss is 'shellfish' (魚介類 sense). Correct rendering is 'marisco'. The pt list must mirror the en list.

findings.issue: 'Infante' in modern pt-BR primarily means a royal prince (or an infantry soldier); as 'small child' it is dated/literary and reads as a false cognate of 'infant'. Natural pt-BR for this sense is 'bebê' or 'criança pequena'.
notes: 'Infante' is a real, formal pt-BR word for a young child (legal/pediatric register), a true cognate, and fits 児's formal compound usage. Suggested 'bebê' would over-narrow the meaning.
'Infante' is dated/formal but correct pt for 'criança' (first sense in Houaiss/Aurélio) and a true cognate of 'infant' here. 'Criança' already leads; register complaint only.

findings.issue: Extra gloss 'azeite' is misleading: bare 'azeite' in pt-BR means olive oil specifically, but 油 means oil in general (olive oil is オリーブ油). EN correctly has only 'oil'; the pt list should match with just 'óleo'.
notes: EN fact layer has only 'oil'; 'azeite' unqualified means olive oil in modern pt-BR (オリーブ油), a narrower sense 油 alone doesn't carry. Drop it, keep 'óleo'.
Bare 'azeite' = olive oil specifically in pt-BR; 油 is oil in general (incl. 石油). Extra hyponym gloss absent from en teaches a wrong equivalence. Keep only 'óleo'.

findings.issue: 'Singrar' is correct but literary/archaic in pt-BR and out of place in a learner-facing gloss list; 'velejar' is the natural everyday equivalent of 'sail'.
notes: 'Singrar' is literary but correct and current pt-BR; register preference alone is not a defect. 'Velejar' (sail with sails) would be worse for 航, which covers navigation broadly incl. aviation.
'Singrar' is literary but semantically exact. Suggested 'velejar' is worse: it means sail-powered sailing, while 航 covers ship/aircraft navigation generally (航海, 航空).

findings.issue: 'shore' is not a meaning of 陸; shore is 岸. 陸 means land/dry land as opposed to sea (陸地, 陸路, 上陸 = coming onto land). Presenting 'shore' as a core sense misleads learners into confusing 陸 with 岸.
notes: JMdict glosses standalone 陸(りく) as 'land; shore' — 'shore' is source-attested (cf. 上陸/陸に上がる), so the finding's premise ('shore is not a meaning of 陸') is factually wrong; entry is defensible.
No major reference (KANJIDIC2: 'land, six') glosses 陸 as 'shore'; shore is 岸. As one of only two glosses it actively misleads. Fix 'land, dry land' is correct.

findings.issue: 'continente' is the meaning of the compound 大陸, not of 陸 alone, which means terra/terra firme (em oposição ao mar). Also misaligned with the EN list (land/shore).
findings.suggested: terra firme, terra (em oposição ao mar)
notes: 'continente' is unsupported: KANJIDIC2 gives 'land, six', JMdict 'land; shore'. Continent is 大陸, not 陸 alone; as one of only two pt glosses it misleads and misaligns with EN.
'continente' is 大陸, not 陸 alone; also breaks EN/PT parity.

findings.issue: 'ordinary' is the meaning of the compound 普通, not of the character. 普 itself means universal/widespread (普遍, 普及); standard glosses are 'universal, wide(ly), generally'. The primary sense 'universal' is missing.
notes: Japanese kanji dictionaries (Kanjipedia) list なみ・ふだん ('ordinary/usual', 普段・普通) as a sense of the character itself; 'general, widely' already covers KANJIDIC's 'wide(ly), generally/universal'. Defensible.
KANJIDIC2/Heisig/Kodansha gloss 普 as 'universal, widely, generally' (kun あまね/あまねし). 'ordinary' leaks from 普通; core sense 'universal' is missing. Fix is correct.

findings.issue: Mirrors the EN defect: 'comum' renders the compound meaning of 普通, not the character sense. The primary sense 'universal' (普遍, 普及) is missing.
notes: Mirrors the EN verdict: 'comum' reflects a legitimate character sense (なみ・ふだん per Kanjipedia), and 'geral, amplamente' cover the universal/widespread sense. Defensible learner set.
Mirrors the EN defect: 'comum' renders 普通, and 'universal' is missing. Fix 'universal, geral, amplamente' is correct.

findings.issue: 'shameless' (from 厚かましい/厚顔) is a marginal sense presented as one of only two core meanings; the actual secondary core sense 'kind, cordial' (厚意, 温厚, 手厚い) is missing. pt list ('grosso, espesso') also has no counterpart for it.
notes: KANJIDIC2 order: thick, heavy, rich, kind, cordial, brazen, shameless — 'shameless' is the most marginal gloss yet shown as 1 of only 2 meanings, while central 'kind/cordial' (厚意, 温厚) is absent; pt ('grosso, espesso') has no counterpart, confirming misalignment.
'shameless' exists in KANJIDIC2 but is the last-listed marginal sense; the core secondary sense 'kind, cordial' (厚意, 温厚, 手厚い) is absent and PT has no counterpart. Fix matches KANJIDIC ordering.

findings.issue: 'patient' is the meaning of the compound 患者, not of the character 患 itself (KANJIDIC: afflicted, disease, suffer from, be ill). A compound-word meaning is presented as a core character meaning.
notes: KANJIDIC2 3.6.2 (project Layer-A source) glosses 患 as 'afflicted, disease, suffer from, be ill' — no 'patient'. That sense belongs to 患者, listed as the example word in the corpus record itself.
'Patient' is an attested sense of 患 itself (Kanjipedia lists 「患者」の略; cf. standalone 急患 = emergency patient), and kanji glosses are conventionally morpheme-level (cf. 誌 'magazine' in same batch).

findings.issue: 'paciente' mirrors the compound meaning of 患者 rather than the character's own sense (sofrer de doença, aflição); it teaches a compound gloss as a core character meaning.
notes: 'paciente' imports the 患者 compound sense; the character's own senses are adoecer/sofrer/doença-aflição. But 'aflição' alone skews to anguish in pt-BR; 'doença' mirrors KANJIDIC's 'disease' better.
'Paciente' mirrors the defensible en gloss; listed last after 'adoecer, sofrer de', so not taught as the core sense, and it reflects real morpheme usage (患者, 急患, 患部). Correct pt-BR.

findings.issue: 'request' is not a sense of 依 itself; it comes from the compound 依頼, where the 'request' sense belongs to 頼. Dictionaries gloss 依 only as reliant/depend on. Presenting 'request' as a core meaning of this character is misleading.
notes: KANJIDIC2 (Layer-A source) glosses 依 only as 'reliant, depend on, consequently, therefore, due to' — no 'request'; that sense comes from 依頼 via 頼. Suggested fix is correct.
No Layer-A source lists 'request' for 依 (KANJIDIC2: reliant/depend on/due to; WK: reliant/dependent). The sense comes from 依頼 via 頼. Suggested fix 'depend on, rely on' is correct.

findings.issue: 'solicitar' mirrors the incorrect EN sense 'request', which belongs to the compound 依頼 (via 頼), not to 依 itself. Should be removed to match the corrected core sense set.
notes: 'solicitar' mirrors the unsupported EN 'request' sense; corpus's own example words show 依-words mean depend/reliance while 'request' only appears in 依頼. Remove it as suggested.
'solicitar' mirrors the unattested EN 'request' and matches no reliance/basis sense of 依 (cf. 依る, 依存, 依然). Fix 'depender de, contar com' is correct pt-BR.

findings.issue: The pt list gives two synonyms for the same 'bathe' sense (banhar-se / tomar banho) and drops the second core sense in en, 'bask in / be exposed to' (as in 日を浴びる, 注目を浴びる).
notes: en lists two senses (bathe / bask in) but pt duplicates the bathe sense (banhar-se = tomar banho) and drops 'bask in / be showered with' (日を浴びる, 注目を浴びる) entirely — real sense-parity gap.
pt duplicates the 'bathe' sense (banhar-se/tomar banho) and drops the en sense 'bask in' (日を浴びる, 注目を浴びる); Layer-B pt must cover all Layer en senses.

findings.issue: 'economia' (singular) reads as 'economy' in pt-BR and invites confusion with 経(済); the natural word for 'savings' is 'poupança' (or 'economias' in the plural).
notes: Singular 'economia' in a bare gloss list reads as 'economy' (経済) and misleads; the pt-BR word for 'savings' (money set aside) is 'poupança'. Suggested fix 'poupar, guardar, poupança' is correct.
Singular 'economia' reads as 'economy' (経済) in pt-BR, a direct gloss collision; 'poupança' is the natural equivalent of en 'savings' (cf. 貯金 = poupança).

findings.issue: "silent" is not a sense of 沈 itself; it comes from the compound 沈黙 (where 黙 carries 'silence'). The character means sink/be submerged/subside (also 'be depressed' figuratively). The pt list correctly omits it, so EN and pt are also misaligned.
notes: 'silent' is not a sense of 沈 in any authoritative source (KANJIDIC2: sink/submerge/subside/be depressed); it leaks from 沈黙 where 黙 carries 'silence'. EN/pt also misaligned. Suggested fix is sound.
KANJIDIC2 senses for 沈 are sink/be submerged/subside/be depressed; 'silent' belongs to 黙 in 沈黙. pt list omits it, so en is the outlier. Suggested fix uses attested senses.

findings.issue: "mestre" (teacher/expert/master craftsman in pt-BR) is not a sense of 殿, whose senses are palace/hall, lord, and the respectful address -dono ('Mr.'). It misrenders the EN set and teaches a wrong sense.
notes: 'mestre' (teacher/expert) renders no sense of 殿 (palace/lord/-dono address); pt-BR for 'Mr.' is 'senhor'. Suggested 'tratamento respeitoso (-dono)' aligns pt 1:1 with EN and fits batch style.
殿 = palace/hall, lord (tono), honorific -dono ('Mr.'). pt-BR 'mestre' means teacher/expert (師), not any 殿 sense; 'senhor' already covers lord/Mr. Suggested fix is fine.

findings.issue: 'bronze' is not a meaning of 銅; the character means copper (Cu). Bronze is 青銅/ブロンズ — the association comes only from the compound 銅メダル ('bronze medal'). Listing 'bronze' as core misleads learners (e.g., 銅線 = copper wire, not bronze).
notes: KANJIDIC2 (Layer-A source) lists only 'copper'. JMdict's second sense is the qualified 'bronze (medal)' metonymy, not the alloy (=青銅). Bare coequal 'bronze' is misleading; fix to 'copper' is correct.
'bronze' is an attested secondary sense: 銅 alone abbreviates 銅メダル (kokugo dicts: 「銅メダル」の略; JMdict has the abbr sense), and 銅像/銅賞/銅器 render as bronze. Copper listed first; defensible.

findings.issue: Mirrors the EN defect: 'bronze' is not a core sense of 銅 (= cobre). Bronze corresponds to 青銅/ブロンズ; only the compound 銅メダル is rendered as 'medalha de bronze'.
notes: Mirrors the EN defect: authoritative core sense is 'cobre'; 'bronze' exists only as the medal metonymy (medalha de bronze). Fix to 'cobre' is correct.
Mirrors EN: 'bronze' is a real secondary sense (medalha de bronze, estátua de bronze = 銅像); 'cobre' listed first keeps the core meaning primary. Defensible for a learner dictionary.

findings.issue: 'enlatado' means canned food/goods (the sense of the compound 缶詰), not the container itself. 缶 means the can/tin; presenting 'enlatado' as a core gloss shifts the sense from container to canned product.
notes: en is 'can, tin' (container only); 'enlatado' means canned goods (the 缶詰 compound sense), not a translation of can/tin, so pt adds a sense absent from Layer A. 'lata' alone is correct.
缶 alone is the container (KANJIDIC: tin can, container); 'enlatado' is the 缶詰 compound sense (canned goods), a genuine sense shift. 'lata' is the right fix.

findings.issue: 'gray' is the meaning of the compound 灰色, not of the character 灰 by itself (in Japanese 灰 alone means ash; KANJIDIC-style glosses are 'ashes'). A compound-word meaning is presented as a core character meaning.
notes: KANJIDIC glosses 灰 as ashes/puckery juice/cremate; no standard kanji source lists 'gray' (that is 灰色). pt side (cinza, cinzas) doesn't mirror gray either. 'ash, ashes' is right.
KANJIDIC glosses 灰 as 'ashes' (+ puckery juice, cremate); 'gray' is the 灰色 compound meaning and is not in the Layer-A source, so it doesn't belong in en.

findings.issue: In Brazilian Portuguese 'confeitaria' primarily means the shop (or the confectioner's craft), not the sweets themselves; as a rendering of 'confectionery' (= sweets collectively) it misleads toward the establishment.
notes: 'Confeitaria' renders the existing en gloss 'confectionery'; pt-BR uses it for the goods domain too (produtos de confeitaria), matching 菓 in compounds like 製菓. Anchored by 'doces, guloseimas', not misleading.
'Confeitaria' also means the craft/products in pt-BR (cf. 製菓), matching EN 'confectionery'; after 'doces, guloseimas' the shop reading isn't the natural takeaway. Defensible.

findings.issue: 'classe de palavra' is nonstandard wording; the established Brazilian grammar term is 'classe gramatical' (or 'classe de palavras').
notes: 'Classe de palavra' (singular) is a calque; established Brazilian terms are 'classe gramatical' / 'classe de palavras'. Below professional standard for a grammar-teaching product. Suggested fix is good.
Singular 'classe de palavra' is nonstandard; BR grammar uses 'classe gramatical' or 'classe de palavras'. Terminology fix, consistent with the project's natural-pt-BR contract.

findings.issue: Unqualified 'mesa' (table in general) is broader than the character's sense: 机 is specifically a desk/study table (dining table is テーブル/食卓). EN correctly has only 'desk'; the pt list over-extends it.
notes: 'Mesa' is a valid pt-BR rendering of 'desk' (mesa de escritório/trabalho); JP-PT dictionaries gloss 机 with 'mesa'. Placed after the precise 'escrivaninha', it's defensible; 'mesa de estudo' would be clunkier.
KANJIDIC itself glosses the character 机 as 'desk, table', so 'mesa' is authoritative-backed; the desk-only restriction applies to the word つくえ, and 'mesa de estudo' is a worse gloss.

findings.issue: 'ticket' is the meaning of the compound 切符, not of 符 itself, yet it is listed first as the core sense. KANJIDIC/standard references gloss 符 as token/sign/mark/tally/charm; 符 alone never means ticket.
notes: No standard reference (KANJIDIC2, Hadamitzky, Nelson) glosses 符 as 'ticket'; that sense belongs to 切符 only. Listing it first is compound contamination of a Layer-A/B fact field.
'ticket' is the 切符 compound meaning, listed first as the core sense; standard refs gloss 符 as token/sign/mark/tally/charm only.

findings.issue: 'bilhete' mirrors the compound-word meaning of 切符 (ticket) rather than a sense of the character 符 itself; should follow the corrected EN sense set (sinal/marca/símbolo).
notes: 'bilhete' mirrors the invalid 'ticket' gloss; pt must track the corrected en sense set (sinal, marca, símbolo).
'bilhete' mirrors the same compound-derived defect into pt-BR; sinal/marca/símbolo is the correct sense set.

findings.issue: 'result' belongs to the compound 結果 (where 果 carries the fruit/result sense); 結 itself means tie/bind/join/conclude. Presenting 'result' as a core sense of 結 misleads learners.
notes: KANJIDIC2 glosses 結 as tie/bind/contract/join/fasten — never 'result'. In 結果, 果 supplies fruit/result; 結 supplies bear/form. 'conclude' (結論, 完結, 契約を結ぶ) is a valid replacement.
No standard reference glosses 結 as 'result'; in 結果 the result sense sits on 果. 'Conclude' (結論/結局/結末) is the attested sense.

findings.issue: 'resultado' reproduces the compound-word meaning of 結果 instead of a sense of 結; should be the 'concluir' sense to match the corrected EN list.
notes: 'resultado' mirrors the invalid 'result' gloss; 'concluir' correctly matches the corrected en list.
'resultado' (noun) unmistakably reproduces the 結果 compound meaning; 'concluir' matches the corrected EN senses.

findings.issue: EN lists three core senses (propose, present, carry) but the pt list drops 'carry' (kun 提げる, as in 手提げ), a distinct sense not covered by propor/apresentar.
notes: en has three senses and readings_fact includes kun さ (提げる 'carry in hand'), but pt drops that sense entirely — a genuine en/pt parity defect. 'carregar (na mão)' is an apt fix.
Real EN/PT parity gap: kun 提げる 'carry in hand' (手提げ) is a distinct core sense in EN but missing from pt; 'carregar (na mão)' is an apt gloss.

findings.issue: EN 'stump' is mistranslated as 'tronco', which means 'trunk' (the meaning of 幹, already glossed 'tronco' in this batch). The correct pt-BR word for a tree stump is 'toco'. As-is it teaches another character's meaning and collides with 幹.
notes: 'Tronco' means trunk (= 幹, glossed 'tronco' at line 302 of this very batch); stump is 'toco' in pt-BR. Real cross-character collision; 'ação, toco, cepa' is correct.
株 never means 'trunk' (that is 幹, glossed 'tronco' in this same batch). Stump = 'toco' in pt-BR; 'cepa' correctly covers stump/strain. 'tronco' is a genuine mistranslation, not a style choice.

findings.issue: 'environment' is the meaning of the compound 環境, not of the character 環 itself, which means ring/circle/link (cf. 循環, 一環). A compound-word sense is presented as a core character meaning and will mislead learners reading 環 in other words.
notes: KANJIDIC2 gives ring/circle/link/wheel for 環; 'environment' is only the 環境 compound sense. But the proposed 'ring, loop, circle' is redundant and mismatches the PT fix.
KANJIDIC-level senses of 環 are ring/circle/link/wheel (わ; 循環, 一環). 'environment' exists only via the compound 環境, where 環 contributes 'encircle'. Suggested 'ring, loop, circle' is acceptable.

findings.issue: 'ambiente' mirrors the compound-derived sense 'environment' (環境); the character 環 itself means anel/círculo/elo. Must be corrected together with the EN list.
notes: 'Ambiente' mirrors the compound-only 環境 sense; 環 itself is anel/círculo/elo (cf. 一環, 循環). Suggested 'anel, círculo, elo' is correct pt-BR and matches the corrected EN list.
'ambiente' is the compound sense of 環境, not of 環. 'anel, círculo, elo' matches the character's real senses (elo = link, cf. 一環) and keeps EN/PT parity with the corrected EN list.

findings.issue: 'finance' is the meaning of the compound 金融, not of the character 融 itself, which means melt/dissolve/fuse (融ける, 融合). A compound-word sense is presented as a core character meaning.
notes: KANJIDIC2 lists only dissolve/melt for 融; 'finance' exists solely via 金融/融資 compounds. 'melt, dissolve, fuse' matches 融ける/融合 and is the right character-level gloss set.
No character dictionary glosses 融 as 'finance'; its senses are melt/dissolve/circulate (融ける, 融合, 融通). 'finance' belongs to 金融. 'melt, dissolve, fuse' is an accurate replacement.

findings.issue: 'finanças' mirrors the compound-derived sense 'finance' (金融); the character 融 itself means derreter/dissolver/fundir. Must be corrected together with the EN list.
notes: 'Finanças' mirrors the compound-only 金融 sense. 'derreter, dissolver, fundir' is accurate pt-BR and stays in parity with the corrected EN list.
'finanças' mirrors the same compound-derived error and must track the EN fix. 'derreter, dissolver, fundir' is correct pt-BR and covers 融合/融ける senses.

findings.issue: 'lunchbox' is the meaning of the compound 弁当 (bento), not a core sense of the character 弁 itself (standard glosses: speech, dialect, valve, petal, discriminate). Presenting a compound-word meaning as a core character meaning is misleading.
notes: 'Lunchbox' is the 弁当 compound gloss, not a sense of 弁 (KANJIDIC: valve, petal, speech, dialect, discriminate); entry's own kun readings (わきま, はなびら, あらそ) confirm no such sense.
No authoritative source glosses 弁 alone as 'lunchbox'; that sense exists only in the compound 弁当. Entry's own readings_fact (はなびら, わきま, かんむり…) shows no lunchbox sense.

findings.issue: 'marmita' mirrors the English 'lunchbox' defect: it renders the compound 弁当, not a sense of the character 弁 itself. Should be removed together with the EN fix.
notes: 'Marmita' translates 弁当, not 弁; must be dropped with the EN fix to keep EN/PT parity. 'fala, dialeto, válvula' is a correct replacement.
'marmita' mirrors the EN defect: it renders 弁当, not any sense of 弁 itself. Remove alongside the EN fix; 'fala, dialeto, válvula' is correct pt-BR.

findings.issue: pt list duplicates the 'colleague' sense ("colega" and "colega de trabalho" are the same sense) and omits the 'official/bureaucrat' sense present in EN and core to this kanji (官僚, 閣僚).
notes: pt renders en 'official' as 'colega de trabalho' (duplicate of 'colega'), losing the bureaucrat sense central to 官僚/閣僚; suggested fix is sound.
pt duplicates the colleague sense and drops 'official' (官僚/閣僚), which EN carries; real sense-coverage gap, and the suggested fix is sound.

findings.issue: pt list gives two synonyms of 'bury' ("sepultar", "enterrar") and omits the 'funeral' sense present in EN and essential for this kanji (葬式, 葬儀).
notes: pt renders en 'funeral' as 'enterrar' (synonym of 'sepultar'), losing the 葬式/葬儀 sense tied to on-reading ソウ; suggested fix is sound.
'sepultar' and 'enterrar' are synonyms for one sense; the 'funeral' sense (葬式/葬儀) present in EN is missing. Suggested 'sepultar, funeral' restores parity.

findings.issue: 'century' is the meaning of the compound 世紀, not of the character 紀 itself; the single kanji means chronicle/account/era/geological period (as in ジュラ紀). pt 'século' mirrors the same compound meaning and should be fixed in parallel.
notes: No kanji dictionary lists 'century' for 紀 alone (KANJIDIC2/Kanjipedia: chronicle, era, geologic period); it's the 世紀 compound sense. 'period' + pt 'período' is a sound fix.
No authoritative source glosses 紀 alone as 'century'; that sense is compound-only (世紀). KANJIDIC: chronicle/account/geologic period. 'period' fix is fine; mirror pt 'século'→'período'.

findings.issue: 'measure' and 'step' are meanings of the compound 措置, not of the character; 措 alone means set aside/place/dispose (KANJIDIC: set aside, give up, suspend). pt 'medida, providência' mirrors the same problem and should follow the fix.
findings.fix: en: 'set aside, give up, suspend' (pt: 'pôr de lado, desistir de, suspender')
notes: KANJIDIC2 gives 'set aside, give up, suspend'; Kanjipedia おく/はからう. 'measure, step' is the 措置 compound meaning, not the character's. Suggested fix matches authoritative senses.
'measure/step' are 措置 compound senses; KANJIDIC gives set aside/give up/suspend. Finding is right but its fix ('dispose, handle') is weakly supported and 'dispose' misreads as 'throw away'.

findings.issue: Standalone 'tentar' will be read by Brazilian learners as 'to try', which is false for 惑; the intended sense is 'to tempt/beguile' (誘惑). Needs disambiguation, e.g. 'seduzir' or 'tentar (seduzir)'.
notes: Bare 'tentar' in a verb gloss list defaults to 'to try' for pt-BR readers — false for 惑. Real learner hazard, needs disambiguation; 'seduzir' or 'tentar (seduzir)' both acceptable.
Bare 'tentar' beside 'duvidar' will be read as 'to try', a false sense for 惑; the tempt/beguile sense needs disambiguation. 'seduzir' (or 'tentar (seduzir)') is an adequate fix.

findings.issue: EN gives the purpose/benefit sense 'for the sake of', but pt renders the causal sense 'because of' ('por causa de'); the core senses do not align. Use a benefit/purpose rendering such as 'em prol de' or 'para o bem de'.
notes: Causal ため is a core sense of 為 (KANJIDIC2 lists 'as a result of'); 'por causa de' is correct. pt array isn't positional anyway (en 'make' vs pt 'servir de'), so no misalignment defect.
為/ため authoritatively carries the causal sense — KANJIDIC lists 'as a result of' — so 'por causa de' is correct and common. Lists are gloss samples, not per-index mirrors (cf. 'servir de' vs 'make').

findings.issue: 'criminal case' is the meaning of the compound 刑事(事件), not of 刑 itself. The character means penalty/punishment/(penal) sentence (cf. 死刑, 実刑, 刑期). Presenting 'criminal case' as a core character meaning is misleading.
notes: 刑 alone means penalty/punishment/sentence (KANJIDIC: 'penalty, sentence, punishment'); 'criminal case' is 刑事事件, a compound-meaning bleed. 'sentence' is a correct replacement.
No standard kanji dictionary (incl. KANJIDIC2: punish/penalty/sentence/punishment) glosses 刑 as 'criminal case'; that sense belongs to 刑事(事件). 'sentence' is the correct missing gloss.

findings.issue: 'caso criminal' mirrors the compound-derived English gloss; 刑 by itself does not mean criminal case. Should render the character's own sense (pena/sentença penal).
notes: 'caso criminal' mirrors the incorrect EN gloss; 刑 itself is pena/sentença penal. 'sentença' is acceptable and keeps parity with EN 'sentence' alongside existing 'pena'.
'caso criminal' inherits the compound-derived error; 'sentença' with 'pena, punição' correctly renders the character's own senses (死刑, 実刑, 刑期).

findings.issue: EN lists 'tail, end' but pt gives two synonyms for tail ('cauda, rabo') and omits the 'end' sense (as in 末尾, 語尾). Alignment gap: replace the duplicate synonym with the missing sense.
notes: EN 'end' is a real KANJIDIC sense (末尾, 語尾) but pt spends both slots on tail synonyms and drops it; Layer-B pt must cover the same senses as EN. 'cauda, fim' fixes it.
PT duplicates the tail sense (cauda/rabo) and drops 'end' (末尾, 語尾), a real en/pt sense misalignment; 'rabo' is also mildly vulgar in pt-BR, so 'cauda, fim' is strictly better.

findings.issue: EN core set is 'board, tray, disk' but pt substitutes 'base' for 'disk', dropping the disk sense (円盤, 序盤/record・disc words) and introducing a sense (基盤) not in the EN list. Align by using 'disco'.
notes: 'base' translates the 基盤 sense absent from the EN list while losing 'disk' (円盤, レコード盤), breaking EN↔PT sense alignment. 'disco' is the correct third item.
'base' introduces a sense (基盤) absent from EN while dropping listed 'disk' (円盤); pt must align with the EN meaning set. 'disco' is the correct fix.

findings.issue: 'caçar' (to hunt) is not a core sense of 獲, which means to catch/capture/acquire (捕獲, 獲得, 漁獲); hunting is 狩. An adjacent/marginal sense is presented as core and can mislead learners.
notes: 獲 means catch/capture/acquire (捕獲, 獲得, 獲物 = the catch); hunting is 狩. 'caçar' is absent from en, misrepresents the kanji, and collides with 狩 for learners. Suggested fix is good.
'caçar' matches no en gloss and no authoritative sense of 獲 (seize/get/acquire; 獲物 = the catch, hunting = 狩); it teaches a wrong mapping. Suggested fix 'capturar, apanhar, obter' is correct.

findings.issue: 'tentar' is ambiguous in a bare gloss list: pt-BR learners will read it as 'to try', not 'to tempt' (誘惑). An unambiguous verb avoids teaching the wrong sense.
notes: Bare 'tentar' defaults to 'to try' for pt-BR readers — a meaning flip; the tempt sense is literary and undisambiguated here. 'seduzir' (or 'atrair') fixes it at zero cost.
'tentar' is the standard pt gloss for 'tempt' (tentação = 誘惑) and is disambiguated by neighboring 'convidar/induzir'; gloss polysemy is normal, and 'seduzir' would add an unwanted erotic slant.

findings.issue: EN core list includes 'distract' (紛らす/気を紛らす), a distinct sense, but pt covers only the mixed-up/confused senses; alignment gap.
notes: 'distract/divert' (紛らす, 気を紛らす) is a distinct, frequent sense present in en and in KANJIDIC's gloss set; pt omits it. Real en/pt alignment gap; 'distrair' is correct.
'distract' is a core sense (KANJIDIC lists it first; 気を紛らす) and appears in the en field; pt drops it, breaking en/pt sense alignment. Adding 'distrair' is the right fix.

findings.issue: EN core list includes 'restrain' (慎む = refrain/abstain, e.g. 口を慎む, 酒を慎む), but pt covers only the careful/prudent senses; alignment gap.
notes: 慎む has a separate refrain/abstain sense (酒を慎む, 口を慎む) reflected by en 'restrain' but uncovered by 'ter cautela, prudente'. 'conter-se' renders it correctly.
慎む has a distinct refrain/abstain sense (口を慎む, 酒を慎む; JMdict sense 2) present in en as 'restrain' but absent from pt; 'conter-se' is an acceptable fix.

findings.issue: 'fuzil' means specifically 'rifle'. 銃 is the generic character for gun/firearm (拳銃 pistol, 小銃 rifle); presenting 'fuzil' as a core meaning teaches an overly narrow sense not matching EN 'gun, firearm'.
findings.fix: Remove 'fuzil' entirely, leaving 'arma de fogo' (covers both EN glosses 'gun' and 'firearm'). Do not add bare 'arma' — it means any weapon, including blades.
notes: 'fuzil'=rifle specifically; 銃 is the generic gun character, so the gloss is wrongly narrow. But bare 'arma' is too broad and redundant beside 'arma de fogo'.
'fuzil' = rifle specifically; matches neither EN gloss (gun, firearm) and misleads for 拳銃-type words. But the proposed fix 'arma' (= weapon in general) over-broadens.

findings.issue: 'relva' is characteristic European Portuguese; Brazilians say 'grama/gramado'. It is also redundant since both 'gramado' and 'grama' are already listed.
notes: 'relva' is the Portugal-standard term, rare/literary in Brazil; project hard rule is pt-BR never pt-PT, and 'gramado'/'grama' already cover the meaning. Suggested fix is correct.
'relva' is everyday pt-PT but bookish/uncommon in Brazil; project has a hard never-pt-PT rule, and 'gramado'/'grama' already cover EN lawn/turf/grass, so it adds nothing.

findings.issue: 'medical examine' is ungrammatical English (adjective modifying a verb).
notes: 'medical examine' (adjective modifying a verb) is ungrammatical English and not a standard KANJIDIC-style gloss; 'examine (medically)' is a sound fix.
'medical examine' is ungrammatical and is not a KANJIDIC gloss (real glosses: checkup, diagnose, examine); clearly below professional quality. Suggested fix is fine.

findings.issue: 'pedir desculpa' (singular) is the typical European Portuguese form; standard Brazilian usage is 'pedir desculpas'.
notes: 'pedir desculpa' is grammatical and current in Brazilian Portuguese (both forms attested in BR dictionaries/media); plural is merely more frequent. Stylistic preference, not a pt-PT error.
'pedir desculpa' is common, natural everyday Brazilian usage (VOLP/Houaiss accept both); the plural is merely more frequent, not a pt-PT marker. Defensible as-is.

findings.issue: 'sóbrio elegante' juxtaposes two adjectives with no connector and reads unnaturally in pt-BR.
notes: 'sóbrio elegante' with no connector reads as a typo-level error in pt-BR; 'sóbrio e elegante' is a natural gloss for the 渋い 'tasteful (subdued)' sense.
'sóbrio elegante' juxtaposes two adjectives with no connector — reads like a copy error, not a valid pt gloss. 'sóbrio e elegante' (or 'elegante (sóbrio)') fixes it.

findings.issue: 'medicamente' is a rare, awkward adverb in pt-BR and can evoke 'medicamento'; 'clinicamente' is the natural choice.
notes: 'medicamente' is vanishingly rare in pt-BR and visually collides with 'medicamento'; 'clinicamente' is the natural adverb and matches the intended sense.
'medicamente' is a near-nonexistent adverb in pt-BR and visually collides with 'medicamento'; 'examinar (clinicamente)' is the natural rendering of the intended sense.

findings.issue: 'welcome' is the meaning of the compound 歓迎, not of the character 歓 itself. Authoritative references (KANJIDIC2, Nelson, Kanshudo) gloss 歓 only as 'delight, joy'; presenting 'welcome' as a core sense misleads learners about what 歓 contributes in compounds.
notes: KANJIDIC2/Nelson gloss 歓 only as delight/joy; the 'welcome' sense of 歓迎 belongs to 迎. 'welcome' is not a character-level sense and misleads on compound decomposition.
KANJIDIC2/Nelson/Halpern gloss 歓 only as 'delight, joy'; 'welcome' comes from 迎 in 歓迎, not from 歓. Suggested fix 'joy, delight' is correct.

findings.issue: 'acolher' mirrors the compound-derived sense 'welcome' (from 歓迎), which is not a core sense of the character 歓 (delight, joy). Should be dropped together with the EN fix to keep alignment.
notes: 'acolher' mirrors the spurious 'welcome' sense (and is a verb among nouns); must be dropped with the EN fix to keep en/pt alignment.
'acolher' mirrors the erroneous 'welcome' gloss; must be dropped with the EN fix to keep locale parity. 'alegria, júbilo' is correct.

findings.issue: 'cordame' is a collective nautical term (a ship's rigging, set of ropes), not a natural rendering of the core sense 'cord'. The natural pt-BR pair for rope/cord is 'corda, cordão'.
notes: 'cordame' is a collective nautical term (ship's rigging), not 'cord'; 縄 denotes an individual rope/cord. 'corda, cordão' correctly mirrors EN 'rope, cord'.
'cordame' is a collective noun (ship's rigging, conjunto de cabos), not a rendering of 'cord'; 'corda, cordão' is the natural pt-BR pair.

findings.issue: 'generally' is the meaning of the compound 大抵 (taitei), not of the character 抵 itself. The character's core senses are resist / reach / touch (抵抗, 抵触, 抵達). A compound-word meaning is being presented as a core character meaning.
notes: 'generally' is the 大抵 compound sense, not a sense of 抵; KANJIDIC2 (Layer-A authority) glosses 抵 as 'resist, reach, touch'. Suggested fix matches it exactly.
KANJIDIC2 (Layer-A ground truth) gives 抵 = resist/reach/touch; 'generally' is the 大抵 compound sense (already in example_words) wrongly promoted to a core meaning, displacing 'touch'.

findings.issue: pt carries the compound-derived sense 'geralmente' (from 大抵) as a core meaning and omits a rendering of the character's real sense 'reach/touch', so it neither matches the character nor covers the corrected EN sense set.
notes: pt carries compound-derived 'geralmente' and omits reach/touch entirely; 'resistir, alcançar, tocar' correctly mirrors the fixed en senses in natural pt-BR.
pt inherits the compound-derived 'geralmente' and omits any rendering of reach/touch, breaking parity with en and with KANJIDIC2; 'resistir, alcançar, tocar' is correct pt-BR.

findings.issue: 'script' is the meaning of the compound word 脚本 (kyakuhon), not of the character 脚 itself. 脚 means leg / lower part / undercarriage / base (of an object). Kanji dictionaries (KANJIDIC) give 'skids, leg, undercarriage, lower part, base' — no 'script'.
findings.suggested: leg, lower part, base (of an object)
findings.fix: leg, lower part, base (of an object)
notes: 'script' belongs to the compound 脚本, not the character; KANJIDIC gives leg/lower part/undercarriage/base. Suggested fix is correct.

No kanji dictionary gives 'script' for 脚; that sense exists only in the compound 脚本. 脚 alone means leg / lower part / support (KANJIDIC: skids, leg, undercarriage, lower part, base). Genuinely misleading.

findings.issue: 'roteiro' mirrors the wrong English sense: it is the meaning of the compound 脚本, not of the kanji 脚, which means perna / parte inferior / base.
notes: 'roteiro' mirrors the same compound-only sense; 脚 itself means perna/parte inferior/base. Suggested pt fix is correct.
'roteiro' mirrors the same error: it translates 脚本, not the character 脚. 'perna, parte inferior, base (de objeto)' is correct pt-BR and matches the en fix.

findings.issue: 'oxygen (in compounds)' is the meaning of the words 酸素/酸化, not of the character; in compounds 酸 overwhelmingly means acid (硫酸, アミノ酸, 胃酸). No standard kanji dictionary lists 'oxygen' for 酸; presenting it as a core sense misleads learners.
notes: 'oxygen' is not a dictionary sense of 酸; even in 酸素 the morpheme means 'acid' (calque of Sauerstoff). In compounds 酸 = acid. Trim to 'acid, sour'.
Finding is factually wrong: Kanjipedia and kokugo dictionaries list 「酸素」の略 as a sense of 酸 (酸化, 酸欠). The '(in compounds)' qualifier makes 'oxygen' defensible and useful for learners.

findings.issue: 'oxigênio (em compostos)' reproduz o sentido do composto 酸素/酸化, não do caractere; em compostos 酸 significa ácido. Should be removed to match the corrected English sense set.
notes: 'oxigênio (em compostos)' repeats the invalid sense; corrected set 'ácido, azedo' matches the fixed English.
Same as the en finding: 'oxigênio (em compostos)' reflects a real, dictionary-attested abbreviation sense of 酸 (酸素/酸欠) and is properly qualified; removal is not required.

findings.issue: Missing the primary sense 'bribe'. The on-reading ワイ appears almost exclusively in bribery vocabulary (賄賂, 収賄, 贈賄), which is the most common use of this kanji; only the kun 賄う 'provide/cover costs' senses are listed.
notes: KANJIDIC2 lists 'bribe' as the primary sense; the on-reading ワイ (present in readings_fact) is used almost only in 賄賂/収賄/贈賄. Omitting it is a real gap.
KANJIDIC2 lists 'bribe' first for 賄; the on ワイ (in readings_fact) exists almost only in 賄賂/収賄/贈賄. Omitting it drops the character's most salient sense — real gap.

findings.issue: Same gap as EN: the core sense 'suborno' (bribe, as in 賄賂/収賄) is missing from the pt-BR list.
notes: Mirrors the EN gap: 'suborno' is the core ワイ-compound sense and is absent from the pt-BR list.
Same gap in pt-BR: 'suborno' missing. Suggested fix 'suborno, prover, cobrir (custos)' is natural pt-BR and correct.

findings.issue: 'persevere' is not a meaning of the character 頑 itself; it comes from the compound 頑張る. The character means stubborn/obstinate/firm (cf. 頑固, 頑丈). Presenting 'persevere' as a core character sense is misleading.
notes: 'Persevere' is unattested for 頑 in KANJIDIC2/Halpern/KLC (stubborn, foolish, firmly); it derives only from 頑張る, itself ateji. Suggested fix 'firm' is supported by kun かたく.
No authoritative source (KANJIDIC2: stubborn/foolish/firmly; Kanjipedia: かたくな・つよい) lists 'persevere'; it leaks from 頑張る where 頑 is ateji. Misleading as a character sense.

findings.issue: 'persistir' mirrors the incorrect EN sense 'persevere' (from the compound 頑張る), which is not a meaning of the character itself.
notes: 'Persistir' copies the invalid EN sense and is a verb wedged into an adjective list (teimoso, obstinado); replacement 'firme' is correct.
'persistir' mirrors the unsupported EN gloss. 'teimoso, obstinado, firme' is accurate (頑固/頑丈/頑強) and good pt-BR.

findings.issue: 鶴 means crane (Grus), pt 'grou'. 'Garça' is a heron/egret (family Ardeidae), a different bird that corresponds to the kanji 鷺, not 鶴. Listing 'garça' teaches a false meaning.
notes: 鶴/つる is the crane (Grus) = pt 'grou'; 'garça' is heron/egret (Ardeidae) = 鷺/さぎ. En gloss is only 'crane (bird)', so 'garça' is a factual mistranslation in a Layer-B fact field, not a stylistic choice.

鶴 (tsuru) is the crane, Gruidae = pt 'grou'. 'Garça' (heron/egret, Ardeidae) is a different bird with its own kanji 鷺 (sagi); en field says only 'crane (bird)', so 'garça' adds a false meaning. Fix to 'grou' is correct.

findings.issue: 'courtyard' is the meaning of the visually similar kanji 庭 (garden/yard), not 廷. KANJIDIC glosses 廷 as courts/imperial court/government office (cf. 法廷, 宮廷); it never means a physical courtyard.
notes: KANJIDIC2 glosses 廷 as 'courts, imperial court, government office'; 'courtyard' belongs to 庭. Batch's own pt list (corte, tribunal) already lacks the courtyard sense.
KANJIDIC2 glosses 廷 as courts/imperial court/government office; 'courtyard' is the first gloss of 庭, not 廷. Batch pt list (corte, tribunal) already lacks it — only en is wrong.

findings.issue: 'bored' is the meaning of the compound 退屈, not of the character 屈 itself (dictionaries gloss 屈 as yield/bend/flinch/submit). Presenting it as a core sense misleads readings of 屈服, 屈折, 不屈.
notes: KANJIDIC2 glosses 屈 as 'yield, bend, flinch, submit' — no 'bored'. That sense comes only from the compound 退屈; kun かがむ confirms the bend/crouch core.
KANJIDIC2 glosses 屈 as yield/bend/flinch/submit; 'bored' is a compound-level sense of 退屈 only, not a character gloss. Suggested fix matches ground truth.

findings.issue: 'entediado' mirrors the incorrect EN sense 'bored', which belongs to the compound 退屈, not to the character 屈; the pt list should render bend/yield/submit only.
notes: 'entediado' mirrors the spurious en 'bored'; character-level senses are dobrar/ceder/submeter-se. Suggested pt fix is natural pt-BR.
'entediado' mirrors the invalid en sense 'bored'; character-level pt should be dobrar/ceder/submeter-se. Suggested fix is natural pt-BR.

findings.issue: 'Contradiction' is the meaning of the compound 矛盾 (mujun, 'halberd-shield'), not of the character 盾 itself, which means only 'shield' (kun: たて). Presenting a compound's meaning as a core character meaning misleads learners (e.g. 後ろ盾 'backer' has nothing to do with contradiction).
notes: No dictionary (KANJIDIC2, Jisho) lists 'contradiction' for 盾; that sense exists only in the compound 矛盾. Character glosses are shield/escutcheon/pretext.
No authoritative source lists 'contradiction' for 盾 alone (KANJIDIC: shield, escutcheon, pretext); that sense exists only in the compound 矛盾. Compound meaning leaked into character gloss.

findings.issue: 'Contradição' mirrors the compound 矛盾's meaning, not the character's. 盾 by itself means only 'escudo'; the pt list must be corrected together with the EN list.
notes: 'Contradição' mirrors the EN defect; 盾 alone is only 'escudo'. Must be fixed together with the EN list.
'Contradição' mirrors the same compound-meaning leak from 矛盾; 盾 alone is only 'escudo'. Must be fixed together with the EN list.

findings.issue: 'Sumo ring' is the meaning of the compound 土俵 (dohyō), not of 俵 itself. 俵 (たわら) means straw bag/bale (also a counter for bags); the ring is named after the bales that border it. Compound meaning presented as a core character meaning.
notes: KANJIDIC2/Jisho give bag/bale/sack (+counter) for 俵; 'sumo ring' is exclusively the compound 土俵. Compound meaning wrongly promoted to character meaning.
俵 (たわら) = straw bag/bale + counter for bags. Even in sumo, 俵 alone denotes the bales bordering the ring; the ring is 土俵. 'Sumo ring' is a compound meaning, not a character meaning.

findings.issue: 'Ringue de sumô' renders the compound 土俵's meaning, not the character's. 俵 alone means saco/fardo de palha; correct together with the EN list.
findings.current: saco de palha, fardo, ringue de sumô
notes: 'Ringue de sumô' mirrors the EN defect; 俵 alone is saco/fardo de palha. Fix together with the EN list.
'Ringue de sumô' mirrors the 土俵 compound meaning; 俵 alone is saco/fardo de palha. Fix together with EN.

findings.issue: False cognate: English 'futile' (in vain, pointless — as in 虚しい) is not pt-BR 'fútil', whose dominant sense is 'frivolous/trivial' (cf. 'motivo fútil'). A learner would attach the wrong sense 'frivolous' to 虚. Use 'vão' (em vão) or 'inútil'.
notes: Genuine false cognate: pt-BR 'fútil' dominantly means frivolous/trivial (motivo fútil), a sense 虚 lacks. 'Vão' correctly renders the vain/in-vain sense of 虚しい.
Real false friend: pt-BR 'fútil' dominantly means frivolous/trivial (motivo fútil), not 'in vain' as EN 'futile'/虚しい. Misleads learners; 'vão' is the correct rendering.

findings.issue: 'Gorro' (winter beanie) and 'touca' (swim/shower cap, bonnet) evoke modern casual knit/cloth caps and distort the sense of 冠 (crown, traditional/ceremonial headgear, kanmuri). A neutral rendering of 'cap, headgear' fits better.
notes: 'Gorro' (beanie) and 'touca' (swim cap) name modern casual garments 冠 never denotes (王冠, 冠位, kanmuri = ceremonial headdress); 'coroa, adorno de cabeça' is accurate.
冠 never denotes a beanie or swim cap (that field is 帽子); it is a crown/ceremonial headpiece. 'Gorro/touca' is a mechanical cap/headgear rendering teaching wrong referents. Suggested fix is apt.

findings.issue: 'Refogar' means to saute (fry lightly in oil/fat), i.e. 炒める, not 煮る. 煮 means to cook in liquid (boil/simmer); listing 'refogar' teaches a false cooking technique for this character.
notes: 'Refogar' = sauté in fat (炒める), never boiling/simmering; 煮's kun readings (に-) all denote cooking in liquid. Suggested 'cozinhar em fogo brando' correctly covers the 'simmer' sense.
Refogar = saute in oil (炒める), incompatible with 煮 (cook in liquid); contradicts the entry's own 'cozinhar (em água)'. Suggested 'cozinhar em fogo brando' correctly fills the 'simmer' slot.

findings.issue: 'Fictional' is the meaning of the compound 架空 (kakuu), not of the character 架 itself, which means hang/span/erect/frame/rack. A compound-word sense is presented as a core character meaning.
notes: KANJIDIC2 gives 架 = erect/frame/mount/support/shelf/construct; 'fictional' exists only via the compound 架空 and misleads on 書架/十字架/担架. 'frame; rack' is an attested core sense.
KANJIDIC gives 架 = erect/frame/mount/support/shelf/construct; 'fictional' only arises from the compound 架空. Compound sense wrongly promoted to character meaning; 'frame; rack' is a sound replacement.

findings.issue: 'Fictício' mirrors the compound-word sense of 架空, not a sense of the character 架 (pendurar/erguer/armação). Should be replaced by the frame/rack sense to match the corrected EN list.
notes: 'Fictício' mirrors the 架空 compound sense, not a character-level meaning; replacing with 'armação; suporte' keeps PT parallel to the corrected EN list and is natural pt-BR.
'Fictício' mirrors the 架空-only sense and must track the corrected EN list; 'armação; suporte' is accurate, natural pt-BR for the frame/rack/mount sense.

findings.issue: "represa" means dam/reservoir (a barrier impounding water), not what 堤 denotes: the earthen bank/levee itself (堤防, 土手). EN list (embankment, dike, levee) is correct; "represa" introduces a wrong sense in pt.
notes: 'represa' = dam/reservoir, a sense absent from the EN glosses (embankment/dike/levee); dam is 堰堤/ダム, not bare 堤. 'dique, aterro' covers all three EN senses correctly.
'Represa' = dam/reservoir (barragem/açude), not the earthen bank 堤 denotes; wrong sense vs EN 'embankment/dike/levee'. Fix 'dique, aterro' is correct.

findings.issue: "bacia geográfica" over-narrows EN "basin": the character-level sense is the shallow vessel/bowl; the geographic-basin sense exists only in the compound 盆地. Plain "bacia" matches the EN gloss without misleading.
notes: 'bandeja' already covers the vessel sense; the only 'basin' a learner meets for 盆 is 盆地 (geographic). Plain 'bacia' would suggest washbasin, which 盆 never means in Japanese. Defensible as-is.
'Bacia geográfica' is a defensible disambiguation: 盆's basin sense appears in 盆地/海盆 (geographic); plain 'bacia' is ambiguous and 'bandeja' already covers the vessel sense.

findings.issue: 'Polite' is the meaning of the compound 丁寧, not of the character 寧 itself; character-level glosses are 'peaceful, rather, preferably'. A compound's meaning is presented as a core character meaning.
notes: Major JP kanji dictionaries (Daijisen kanji entry, Kanjipedia) list ねんごろ 'courteous' as a character-level sense of 寧 (example: 丁寧). 'Polite' is attested, not compound-only; defensible gloss.
KANJIDIC2/Unicode gloss 寧 as 'rather, preferably, peaceful, quiet, tranquility' — no 'polite'. That sense belongs to the word 丁寧; compound leakage into a character-level fact field is a real defect.

findings.issue: 'Cortês' mirrors the defective EN gloss 'polite', which belongs to the compound 丁寧, not to 寧 itself. Should be dropped together with the EN fix.
notes: 'Cortês' correctly mirrors the defensible EN 'polite' (ねんごろ sense attested at character level in Kanjipedia/Daijisen); nothing to drop.
'Cortês' mirrors the invalid EN gloss 'polite' (sense of 丁寧, not 寧). Drop it together with the EN fix; 'tranquilo, antes (preferência)' is correct.

findings.issue: 'Porcelana' (porcelain) is the sense of 磁 (磁器); 陶 denotes pottery/earthenware (陶器). The EN pair 'pottery, ceramics' is not covered — pt introduces a different character's sense as core.
notes: KANJIDIC2 itself glosses 陶 as 'pottery, porcelain'; everyday 陶器 covers china broadly. 'Porcelana' is source-backed. Suggested 'olaria' (pottery workshop) would be worse pt-BR.

Premise is wrong: KANJIDIC2 glosses 陶 as 'pottery, porcelain' (cf. 陶磁器, 陶芸). 'Porcelana' is authoritative for 陶, not exclusive to 磁; 'cerâmica' already covers pottery/ceramics. 'Olaria' would be worse.

findings.issue: 'Margem' (riverbank/page margin) is not a natural rendering of EN 'side' for 傍 (beside/vicinity); it injects an edge/bank connotation. 'Lado' is the direct equivalent.
notes: Loose but defensible: 傍 covers the margin/edge domain (傍注 'marginal note', 傍線, 路傍 'à margem do caminho'). Minor stylistic quibble; suggested 'lado' merely duplicates 'ao lado'.
'Margem' reads as riverbank/page margin (岸/縁/端), a sense absent from 傍 and from the EN glosses it must track; misleads production. 'Lado' correctly renders 'side'.

findings.issue: 'pendurar' means to hang something UP (attach on a hook/wall, cf. 掛ける), while 垂 means to hang DOWN / droop / dangle. The intransitive-downward verb in pt-BR is 'pender'.
notes: 'pendurar' is transitive 'hang up' (= 掛ける/吊る), contradicting en 'hang down/droop' and colliding with other kanji glosses; intransitive 'pender' is the correct pt-BR match.
'pendurar' is transitive hang-up (= 掛ける/吊るす); 垂 is intransitive droop/hang down (垂れる, 垂直). 'pender' is the correct pt-BR verb and the suggested fix is good.

findings.issue: 'alinhavar' specifically means to baste/tack (loose temporary stitching), a narrow technique, not the general sense of 'stitch'. 'suturar' (or just 'costurar' alone) better matches the EN core senses, incl. stitching a wound (傷を縫う).
notes: 'alinhavar' means baste/tack (しつけ), a mistranslation of en 'stitch'; 'suturar' fits 傷を縫う/縫合 and complements 'costurar'. 'costurar, dar pontos' also acceptable.
'alinhavar' = baste (仮縫い/しつけ), a narrow prep technique; as the parallel gloss for 'stitch' it mistranslates. 'costurar, suturar' matches 縫's real range incl. 縫合/傷を縫う.

findings.issue: 'todavia' in pt-BR means 'however/nevertheless' (a false cognate of Spanish 'todavía' = 'still'). 猶 (なお) means 'still/yet (even now)', which 'ainda' already covers; 'todavia' teaches a contrastive-conjunction sense the character does not have.
findings.fix: Replace 'todavia' with 'mesmo agora' (or drop it, since 'ainda' already covers still/yet). Do not use 'ainda assim' — it is concessive ('even so') and reintroduces the same wrong contrastive sense.
notes: Modern pt-BR 'todavia' is adversative ('however'), a sense 猶/なお lacks; the en source ['still','yet','like'] has no contrastive gloss, so it's a real mistranslation of temporal 'yet'.

pt-BR 'todavia' is only an adversative conjunction (= contudo/porém); 猶/なお is temporal 'still, yet (even now)' plus 'furthermore/like' — classic Spanish 'todavía' false cognate, so the gloss is wrong.

findings.issue: 扉 (tobira) means the door leaf itself and, figuratively, a book's title page. 'batente' in pt-BR is the door jamb/frame stop, not the door — a wrong object — and the curated EN sense 'title page' has no pt counterpart.
notes: 'batente' is the jamb/stop in pt-BR (leaf sense is marginal), and the curated 'title page' sense has no pt counterpart. 'porta, página de rosto' is correct ('folha de rosto' also fine).
'batente' is the jamb/frame stop in pt-BR, not the door leaf; and EN sense 'title page' (本の扉) lacks any pt counterpart. Suggested 'porta, página de rosto' is correct.

findings.issue: 紡 means to spin thread/yarn (紡ぐ, 紡績). 'weave' is the meaning of 織, a distinct textile process; presenting it as a core meaning conflates the two characters.
notes: 紡 = spin/spinning (KANJIDIC2); weaving is 織 — cf. 紡織 'spinning and weaving' contrasting the two. Figurative 紡ぐ 'spin a tale' doesn't justify bare 'weave' as a core meaning.
