紡 is uniformly glossed 'spinning/spin' (KANJIDIC2 etc.); textile 'weave' is 織. Bare 'weave' conflates the two, but the proposed fix duplicates the same lemma.

findings.issue: 'tecer' means to weave (織), not to spin. The correct pt-BR verb for 紡 is 'fiar' (already listed); 'tecer' teaches the wrong process.
notes: 'tecer' = to weave = 織る; 紡ぐ = 'fiar'. Same conflation as the en finding; dropping 'tecer' is correct.
'tecer' = to weave = 織る, the wrong textile process; 'fiar' alone is the correct pt-BR gloss and matches the corrected en field.

findings.issue: 'ave' alone means any bird, which is the meaning of 鳥, not 鶏. The EN 'fowl' implies domestic poultry; the overbroad pt gloss invites 鶏/鳥 confusion.
notes: 'ave' unqualified is the gloss of 鳥 and misdefines 鶏 by genus. 'galinha, frango' fixes it; 'galinha, ave doméstica' would map 'fowl' even more closely, but the suggestion is acceptable.
'ave' means any bird (= 鳥, an N5 corpus entry), losing the domesticity of 'fowl' and colliding with 鳥's gloss. 'galinha, frango' is natural, accurate pt-BR.

findings.issue: 'masterpiece' is the meaning of the compound 傑作, not of the character 傑 itself (which means excel/outstanding; outstanding person, hero). Presenting it as a core sense of the single kanji is misleading.
notes: No authoritative source (KANJIDIC2, Kanjipedia, KKLD) lists 'masterpiece' for 傑 alone; that sense is compound-only (傑作). 'hero' (豪傑/女傑) is a valid attested sense.
No character dictionary (KANJIDIC2, Kanjipedia, Nelson) glosses 傑 as 'masterpiece'; that sense belongs to the compound 傑作. Character senses are excel/outstanding + outstanding person (hero).

findings.issue: 'obra-prima' mirrors the compound-derived English gloss 'masterpiece' (from 傑作); it is not a sense of the character 傑 alone and should be dropped for alignment with the corrected EN list.
notes: 'obra-prima' only mirrors the invalid 'masterpiece' gloss; must follow the EN fix. 'sobressair, excelente, herói' is correct, natural pt-BR.
'obra-prima' only mirrors the compound-derived EN error; with 'masterpiece' removed, pt must align. 'sobressair, excelente, herói' is a correct pt-BR rendering of the attested senses.

findings.issue: Spelling error: 'repártição' has a spurious acute accent on the first 'a'. The correct Brazilian Portuguese spelling is 'repartição'.
notes: Line 543 reads 'repártição oficial'. 'repártição' is not a Portuguese word; the correct spelling is 'repartição' (no accent on the first 'a'). Genuine typo, suggested fix is correct.
File line 543 has 'repártição oficial'; 'repártição' is a misspelling — correct pt-BR is 'repartição'. Suggested fix is correct.

findings.issue: Redundant duplication: the pt list contains the same word in singular and plural ('laticínio', 'laticínios'). One entry should be kept (the plural 'laticínios' is the usual form for 'dairy products').
notes: pt list is ['laticínio','laticínios'] — same lexeme twice, differing only in number, adding zero information (en side has just 'dairy'). Keeping 'laticínios' (usual collective form, e.g. 'setor de laticínios') is the right fix.
pt list is ['laticínio','laticínios'] — same lexeme twice (singular/plural), a dedup artifact, not two senses. Keeping 'laticínios' matches en 'dairy' (collective).

findings.issue: 'Reward' is not a core meaning of 褒 itself (KANJIDIC/Unihan: praise, extol, commend; 褒める = to praise). The 'reward' sense comes from compounds like 褒美/褒賞 and is misleading as a standalone core sense.
notes: No authority (KANJIDIC2 'praise, extol'; Unihan 'praise, commend, honor, cite'; Halpern/Henshall/Nelson) lists 'reward'; that sense is compound-only (褒美/褒賞). Kun ほ.める confirms praise-only.
KANJIDIC2 ('praise, extol'), Unihan ('praise, commend, honor, cite') and 漢和 sources list no 'reward' sense; it belongs to 褒美/褒賞 as whole words. Violates Layer-A provenance.

findings.issue: 'Recompensar' mirrors the defective English sense 'reward', which is compound-derived (褒美/褒賞), not a core meaning of the character; should follow the corrected EN senses (praise/extol).
notes: 'Recompensar' inherits the defective EN gloss and must track the corrected senses; 'elogiar, exaltar' is valid pt-BR ('elogiar, louvar' equally fine).
'Recompensar' inherits the compound-derived EN error; 褒める never means recompensar. 'Elogiar, exaltar' is sound pt-BR ('enaltecer' also fine).

findings.issue: 'Gunpowder' is not a meaning of 硝 itself; standard references (KANJIDIC2, Unihan) gloss it only as nitrate/saltpeter/niter. Gunpowder is 火薬; 硝 merely appears in related compounds like 硝煙. Presenting it as a core sense misleads learners.
notes: KANJIDIC2/Unihan gloss 硝 as nitrate/saltpeter/niter only; even Japanese kokugo dictionaries define it as 火薬の原料 (raw material FOR gunpowder), not gunpowder itself (火薬). Extra sense is unsupported.
Verified vs project KANJIDIC2 3.6.2: gloss is 'nitrate, saltpeter' only. Gunpowder is 火薬; 硝 alone means saltpeter/nitrate. Listing it as a core sense contradicts the Layer-A source.

findings.issue: Mirrors the EN defect: 'pólvora' (gunpowder) is not a sense of 硝, which means salitre/nitrato. Should be removed along with EN 'gunpowder'.
notes: Follows from the EN verdict: 'pólvora' overstates 硝, which names the nitrate compound, not the explosive. 'salitre, nitro' is correct; add 'nitrato' if EN gains 'nitrate'.
Mirrors the EN defect: 'pólvora' (gunpowder) is not a sense of 硝 per KANJIDIC2/Unihan; drop it alongside EN 'gunpowder'. 'salitre, nitro' remains correct pt-BR.

findings.issue: EN core set includes 'quit, resign', but all three pt terms (demitir, destituir, afastar) render only the transitive 'dismiss/remove from office' sense; the quit/resign sense is entirely unrepresented in pt.
notes: Real parity gap: kun や(める) makes quit/resign a core sense, but bare 'demitir' means to fire, and 'destituir'/'afastar' are also transitive removal. 'renunciar' restores the resign sense; fix is good.
EN is 2/3 quit/resign (matches kun や.める), but demitir/destituir/afastar are all transitive 'remove from office'. The quit sense is unrepresented; 'renunciar' (or 'demitir-se') fixes it.

findings.issue: EN lists three core senses (core, wick, pencil lead) but the pt list covers only two; the very common 'lead (of a pencil)' sense (e.g. シャープの芯) has no pt rendering — 'núcleo' does not convey pencil lead in Portuguese, which is 'grafite'.
notes: pt omits the 'lead (of a pencil)' sense that the entry's own EN list asserts; pt-BR for pencil lead is 'grafite', which neither 'núcleo' nor 'pavio' conveys. Suggested fix is correct pt-BR and matches batch style.
EN lists 3 senses but PT only 2; the very common pencil-lead sense (鉛筆の芯) has no pt gloss — 'núcleo' doesn't mean pencil lead, pt-BR uses 'grafite'. Suggested fix is correct.

findings.issue: EN says 'visit a shrine' but pt says 'visitar um templo' (temple). In Japanese-course context shrine (神社) = 'santuário' and temple (寺) = 'templo'; the pt should match the EN sense or cover both.
notes: Locale-parity break: en Layer-A says 'shrine' (santuário) but pt says 'templo' (temple=寺). Distinction is pedagogically load-bearing in JP courses. Suggested 'santuário/templo' is acceptable since 詣 covers both.
pt 'templo' mismatches en 'shrine'; pt-BR pedagogy distinguishes santuário (神社) vs templo (寺). 詣's range covers both, so 'visitar um santuário/templo' is a sound fix.

findings.issue: EN 'audience (with royalty)' rendered as 'audiência (com nobreza)'. 'Nobreza' means nobility, not royalty, and '(com nobreza)' can also read adverbially as 'nobly'. 'Realeza' is the faithful term.
notes: 'Nobreza'=nobility, not royalty; and article-less 'com nobreza' idiomatically reads adverbially ('nobly'). 'audiência (com a realeza)' is the faithful, unambiguous rendering.
'nobreza' = nobility, not royalty; and article-less 'com nobreza' defaults to the adverbial 'nobly' reading in pt-BR. 'audiência (com a realeza)' is faithful and unambiguous.

findings.issue: 'once' is the meaning of the compound 一旦 (ittan), not of the character 旦 itself. Standard kanji references gloss 旦 only as daybreak/dawn/morning. Presenting 'once' as a core character meaning is misleading.
notes: No major reference (KANJIDIC2, Nelson, Halpern, Kanjipedia) glosses 旦 as 'once'; that sense belongs only to the compound 一旦. Suggested 'dawn, daybreak, morning' matches kun readings あさ/あした.
KANJIDIC2/Nelson gloss 旦 as daybreak/dawn/morning only; 'once' belongs to the compound 一旦. Kun readings あさ/あした in this very entry support 'morning'. Suggested fix is correct.

findings.issue: 'uma vez' mirrors the English 'once', which belongs to the compound 一旦, not to the character 旦. Should be replaced with a true character sense.
notes: 'uma vez' mirrors the same 一旦-only sense; not a character meaning. 'amanhecer, alvorada, manhã' correctly mirrors the fixed EN list.
'uma vez' inherits the 一旦 compound sense; not a character meaning. 'amanhecer, alvorada, manhã' is natural pt-BR and mirrors the corrected en.

findings.issue: 'bexiga' primarily means 'bladder' in modern pt-BR; its 'smallpox' sense is archaic/dated. As a core gloss it will mislead learners into associating 痘 with the bladder. 'varíola' alone (or 'varíola, pústula') is safer.
notes: 'bexiga' reads as 'bladder' in modern pt-BR (smallpox sense is dated), inviting a false 痘=bladder link. But dropping to 'varíola' alone loses the generic pox/pustule sense in EN.
'bexiga' = smallpox is dated/popular; modern pt-BR reads it as bladder/balloon, creating a false association for a disease kanji. But dropping to 'varíola' alone loses the 'pox' sense.

findings.issue: EN lists 'sober up' as a core sense (cf. 酔いが醒める; radical 酉 relates to alcohol), but the pt list only covers the wake/awaken sense with two synonyms. Alignment gap.
notes: 'Sober up' is a genuine core sense of 醒 (酉 radical; 酔いが醒める; KANJIDIC2 lists it) and is in the EN list; pt omits it while duplicating the wake sense. 'ficar sóbrio' is a correct fix.
en lists 'sober up' (real sense: 酉 radical, 酔いが醒める, KANJIDIC) but pt omits it; every other batch item has en/pt sense parity. 'ficar sóbrio' is fine pt-BR.
